_note: Hand-curated canonical-edition overrides consulted by stage 04's edition dedup (utils.canonical_edition_tcps). Default policy keeps the EARLIEST DATED edition of a work; entries here force a specific TCP instead. For Shakespeare, the choice follows the New Oxford Shakespeare: the version underlying the Modern Critical Edition text is canonical, so where the corpus offers only a 'bad' quarto/octavo and the Folio, the Folio (nearest witness to the MCE base text) is kept. 'year' supplies a working date for the kept text when the TCP itself is undated (Folio items) — FIRST-PERFORMANCE dating, not print dating (the Folio's print date is 1623); it is written into the derived clustering table only, never into source metadata. APPROVED by Heejin 2026-07-07 ('keep, with explicit note') — see PROVENANCE_LOG.md section 4e. Entries marked confirm=true are two-text plays where the NOS MCE choice should be double-checked against the edition itself.

Hamlet.basis: NOS MCE base is Q2 (not in corpus); Folio is the nearest witness. Q1 (1603) is the memorial/early short text.

Romeo and Juliet.basis: NOS MCE base is Q2 1599 (not in corpus); Folio nearest. Q1 1597 is the short 'bad' text.

The Merry Wives of Windsor.basis: NOS MCE base is F; Q 1602 is the short 'bad' text.

3 Henry the Sixth.basis: NOS MCE base is F (Richard Duke of York O 1595 is the short text).

King Lear.basis: Two-text play; F-based Tragedy taken as the MCE reading text.

Othello.basis: Two-text play; F contains ~160 lines absent from Q 1622; F taken as MCE base.

Richard the Third.basis: Q1 1597 kept (earliest dated); NOS treats the Q tradition as the theatrical text. Confirm against MCE.

Troilus and Cressida.basis: Q 1609 kept (earliest dated). Confirm MCE base (Q vs F) against the edition.
